_why: THE ARRANGEMENT IS ITSELF A FINDING, so it lives here and not in a template.
kosina.json is built by tools/kosina.py out of the GEDCOM and the register
notes, and it is a flat list: six people read out of Kranj-Smartin, five more
of the same household, ten from the family tree. What it does NOT hold is the
SHAPE — that Matthaeus is Franz's brother and not his father, that the line
runs through Gertraud and not through her brother Johann, that Elisabeth,
Maria and Valentin are Franz and Maria's children and so Gertraud's brother
and sisters. Every one of those is a conclusion somebody reached from a
document, several of them on 22 September 2026 and one of them a retraction
of the day before. That is evidence, and the estate's rule is that evidence
lives where a tool can read it.
HAND-KEPT. kosina.py must not write this file and does not; it would have
nothing to say about it. Add a row here when the registers give another
generation, and the page draws it without being edited.
HOW A ROW NAMES A PERSON. `found` is a slug in kosina.json's `above` or
`household` — a person read out of a register, whose page is /found/<slug>/.
`person` is a GEDCOM id in people.json — somebody the family tree holds,
whose page is /people/<slug>/. A row uses whichever applies to each side,
and the page resolves both; nothing here repeats a name or a date the two
data files already carry, except where a register gives a fuller form than
the tree does.
`cite` lists the slugs whose `what` and `cite` from kosina.json belong in
this row's evidence fold, so a citation keeps the name it was written for.
